channel.title: English in a minute ☕ — grammar, typical mistakes and practical tips
channel.description: Free, practical articles for everyone learning English — common mistakes, grammar made simple and the things textbooks don't tell you.

item.title: Very good for everything? 20 words and phrases for more natural English
item.description: Why saying very good about everything sounds flat, and what to say instead — about food, people, work and in conversation, with examples and a short quiz.

item.title: Reported speech explained simply — how to pass on what someone said
item.description: Reported speech made simple: when the tense changes, how to report questions and orders, and why we say told me, not said me — with examples and a test.

item.title: Cambridge B2 First and C1 Advanced — what they are and who needs them
item.description: Cambridge B2 First (FCE) and C1 Advanced (CAE): the exam papers, scoring, who needs which one and how they differ from IELTS — explained simply.

item.title: English in 15 minutes a day — a realistic plan for busy people
item.description: Only 15 minutes a day for English? A weekly plan, what that time will and won't give you, and when you need more time and a teacher.

item.title: English for travel — 38 phrases from the airport to the restaurant
item.description: Travel phrases for passport control, the hotel, restaurants, transport and shops — with typical mistakes and British vs American words.

item.title: English pronunciation — difficult sounds, word stress and how to practise
item.description: English pronunciation made clear: th, w/v, p/t/k, long and short vowels, schwa, silent letters, word stress, the -ed ending and practical ways to practise.

item.title: Gerund or infinitive — to do or doing: which verbs take which form
item.description: enjoy doing or enjoy to do? Which verbs take -ing and which take to + V1, when the meaning changes (stop, remember, try), make/let and typical mistakes.

item.title: Past Simple or Past Continuous — how to tell a story about the past

item.title: Online English level test — 20 questions, A1 to B2

item.title: IELTS Speaking — the three parts, questions and sample answers
item.description: The three parts of IELTS Speaking, the four criteria, typical questions with sample answers, a cue card example and the five most common mistakes.

item.title: Used to, be used to, get used to — the difference explained
item.description: used to, be used to and get used to: meanings, didn't use to, used to or would, the -ing form after be used to, typical mistakes and a short quiz.

item.title: Forgot the word? 15 phrases to keep your English conversation going

item.title: How to remember English words — a system that works
item.description: Why we forget new words and how to learn them so they stick: spaced repetition, active recall, the right kind of flashcard and learning words in context.

item.title: IELTS, TOEFL or Duolingo — which test to choose, and for which country
item.description: IELTS, TOEFL iBT and the Duolingo English Test: length, score scales, result times and who accepts what in Germany, the USA, Canada and the UK.

item.title: Learning English with films and TV series — a method that works

item.title: English conditionals explained simply — all four types on one page
item.description: Zero, first, second and third conditional: the formula, when to use each, the typical mistakes (If I will…, If I would…) and a quick test to check yourself.

item.title: He or she? Why learners mix up gender in English pronouns
item.description: he/she, his/her and it: why learners mix them up in English, the most common mistakes, and a practice method that also works when you are speaking.

item.title: Phrasal verbs explained simply — 25 phrasal verbs for work and conversation
item.description: The 25 most useful phrasal verbs for work and everyday conversation — with plain meanings, examples and typical mistakes. Plus a short quiz at the end.

item.title: Learning English after 40 — is it too late? An honest answer

item.title: English for IT professionals — what a developer really needs
item.description: English for IT professionals online: phrases for standups, Slack and interviews, typical mistakes, and which level you need for remote work abroad.

item.title: How to choose an online English tutor: 10 questions to ask

item.title: The 10 most common mistakes in English — and how to fix them

item.title: English for beginners — where to start: an A1 plan
item.description: Learning English from scratch: your first phrases (be, have, can, like, want), what not to do at the start, and the order of a beginner's first month.

item.title: Business English: 40 phrases for emails, meetings and presentations

item.title: Present Simple or Present Continuous — the difference, with examples

item.title: since or for? How to say how long you've been doing something

item.title: some or any — the rule, the exceptions and a common mistake
item.description: some in positive sentences, any in negatives and questions — plus two exceptions: offers (Would you like some tea?) and any meaning “it doesn't matter which”.

item.title: Present Perfect or Past Simple? How to choose the right tense
item.description: Finished time or a link to now? A simple rule for choosing between the Present Perfect and the Past Simple, plus signal words and an exercise with answers.

item.title: a, an or the — English articles made simple

item.title: in, on or at? Prepositions of time and place

item.title: will, going to or Present Continuous — three ways to talk about the future

item.title: say, tell, speak or talk — four verbs that are easy to mix up
item.description: One rule that covers most cases, the fixed phrases with tell, and what to say on the phone — the difference between say, tell, speak and talk with examples.

item.title: make or do? The difference, with a simple trick

item.title: “I know it all, but I'm afraid to speak” — why it happens and what helps

item.title: How long does it take to learn English — realistic timelines by level

item.title: English for life abroad — at the doctor's, at an office, at work

item.title: Job interview in English — questions, the STAR method and phrases to buy time
item.description: Five questions you will almost certainly be asked in a job interview in English, how to structure your answers with STAR, and what to ask at the end.

item.title: “Tbilisi is too beautiful” — why this is a complaint, not a compliment

item.title: “I'm agree” — one of the most common mistakes English learners make
